questions.question: Who is the chief judge of the Supreme Court of India, as of May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhushan R Gavai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhushan R Gavai** is the current Chief Justice of India (CJI) as of May 2025. He succeeded Dhananjaya Y. Chandrachud, whose tenure as the CJI ended in November 2024.
 
• Justice Gavai is the **52nd Chief Justice of India**. He took the oath of office on **29th November 2024**.
 
• He was appointed as per the seniority convention in the Supreme Court, which is a widely followed practice in the Indian judiciary for appointing the CJI.
 
• Before becoming the Chief Justice of India, Justice Gavai served as a **Judge of the Supreme Court**, where he delivered notable judgments in constitutional, civil, and criminal matters.
 
• Justice Gavai is known for his vast experience and commitment to upholding the principles of the **Indian Constitution**. He is one of the few CJIs from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community, which highlights the inclusivity of the Indian judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice of India (CJI):**

 
 
• The CJI is the **head of the judiciary system** in India and the Supreme Court, which is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution.
 
• The CJI is responsible for the allocation of cases and the constitution of benches to hear them.
 
• He/she also advises the President of India on judicial appointments, including the appointment of other Supreme Court judges.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process of the Chief Justice of India:**
 
 
• The President of India appoints the CJI based on **seniority among the judges** of the Supreme Court.
 
• The process follows the **convention of seniority**, wherein the longest-serving judge of the Supreme Court is appointed as the CJI.
 
 
 
• **Tenure of Justice Bhushan R Gavai:**
 
 
• Justice Gavai's tenure as the CJI is expected to last until **November 2025**, based on the mandatory retirement age of 65 for Supreme Court judges.
 
• He will oversee important decisions and reforms within the judiciary during this period.
 
 
 
• **Notable Contributions of Justice Gavai:**
 
 
• Justice Gavai has delivered several landmark judgments during his tenure as a judge in the Supreme Court.
 
• He is recognized for his commitment to **social justice** and ensuring inclusivity in the judiciary.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Previous Chief Justices:**

 
 
• **Dhananjaya Y. Chandrachud:** Served as the 50th CJI from November 2022 to November 2024.
 
• **Sharad Arvind Bobde:** Served as the 47th CJI from November 2019 to April 2021.
 
• **N.V. Ramana:** Served as the 48th CJI from April 2021 to August 2022.
 
 
 
• **Judiciary in India:**
 
 
• The Indian judiciary is an independent system, with the Supreme Court being the apex court, followed by High Courts and subordinate courts.
 
• The judiciary ensures the enforcement of laws and resolves disputes while safeguarding the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• **Article 124:** Deals with the establishment and composition of the Supreme Court, including the appointment of the CJI and other judges.
 
• **Article 50:** Ensures the separation of the judiciary from the executive in public services.

questions.question:
Consider the following vitamins.

1. Vitamin A

2. Vitamin B6

3. Vitamin C

4. Vitamin D

Which of them is/are fat-soluble?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin A:** It is a **fat-soluble vitamin** that is stored in the liver. It plays a critical role in vision, immune function, and reproduction. *Hence, it is fat-soluble.*
 
• **Vitamin B6:** This vitamin is **water-soluble**, meaning it dissolves in water and is not stored in the body. It is involved in amino acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis. *Hence, it is not fat-soluble.*
 
• **Vitamin C:** Like Vitamin B6, Vitamin C is also **water-soluble**. It is vital for tissue repair, enzymatic production, and immune function. *Hence, it is not fat-soluble.*
 
• **Vitamin D:** Vitamin D is a **fat-soluble vitamin** stored in the body’s fat tissues. It helps in calcium absorption and bone health. *Hence, it is fat-soluble.*
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer includes Vitamin A and Vitamin D.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fat-Soluble Vitamins:**

 
 
• These vitamins include **Vitamin A, D, E, and K**.
 
• They are absorbed along with dietary fats in the intestine and are stored in the liver and fat tissues for future use.
 
• Excessive intake can lead to toxicity because they are not excreted readily.
 
 
 
• **Water-Soluble Vitamins:**
 
 
• These include **Vitamin B-complex (e.g., B6, B12, etc.) and Vitamin C**.
 
• They dissolve in water and are generally not stored in the body; hence, they need to be consumed regularly.
 
• Excess amounts are usually excreted through urine, reducing the risk of toxicity.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin A:**
 
 
• Found in foods such as carrots, sweet potatoes, spinach, and liver.
 
• Deficiency can lead to **night blindness** and immune system issues.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin D:**
 
 
• Produced in the skin upon exposure to sunlight and found in foods such as fish, eggs, and fortified milk.
 
• Deficiency leads to **rickets in children** and **osteomalacia in adults**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Functions of Fat-Soluble Vitamins:**

 
 
• **Vitamin A:** Essential for vision, immune system, and reproduction.
 
• **Vitamin D:** Regulates calcium and phosphate levels in the body for healthy bones and teeth.
 
• **Vitamin E:** Acts as an antioxidant protecting cells from damage.
 
• **Vitamin K:** Plays a vital role in blood clotting and bone metabolism.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Water-Soluble Vitamins:**
 
 
• **Vitamin C:** Important for collagen synthesis, wound healing, and immune support.
 
• **Vitamin B-complex:** Involved in energy production, red blood cell formation, and maintaining the nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Dietary Recommendations:** A balanced diet with a variety of foods ensures adequate intake of both fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins.
 
• **Toxicity Risks:** Overconsumption of fat-soluble vitamins can lead to hypervitaminosis, whereas water-soluble vitamins are generally safer due to excretion.

questions.question: In 2025, which of the following disputes between two countries escalated due to increased military activities near the Line of Actual Control (LAC)?

options.text: India–Sri Lanka dispute over Katchatheevu Island

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India–China dispute in Eastern Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India–China dispute in Eastern Ladakh** escalated significantly in recent years due to tensions near the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**. This region includes areas such as Pangong Lake, Galwan Valley, and Hot Springs.
 
• The confrontation between the two countries intensified in **May 2020**, leading to military clashes in the Galwan Valley in **June 2020**, which resulted in casualties on both sides.
 
• China's infrastructure development and deployment of troops in the region have been key factors contributing to the escalations. Reports indicate the construction of roads, bridges, and military camps along the disputed borders.
 
• India has responded by increasing its military presence, modernizing its infrastructure, and reinforcing its positions along the LAC to counter China's advances.
 
• Several rounds of diplomatic and military-level talks have been held to resolve the conflict, but a permanent solution has yet to be achieved due to differing interpretations of the LAC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Line of Actual Control (LAC):**

 
 
• The LAC is the de facto border between India and China, stretching over **3,488 km**. It is divided into three sectors: Western, Central, and Eastern.
 
• The Western Sector (Ladakh) has been a major flashpoint due to disputes over the **Aksai Chin** region, which is controlled by China but claimed by India.
 
 
 
• **Previous Disputes:**
 
 
• India and China have a long history of border disputes, dating back to the **1962 Sino-Indian War**, where China gained control over Aksai Chin.
 
• Other significant clashes include the **Doklam standoff** in **2017**, near the India-Bhutan-China trijunction.
 
 
 
• **Efforts for Resolution:**
 
 
• India and China have conducted several rounds of military and diplomatic talks, including the **Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC)** and Corps Commander-level meetings.
 
• Despite partial disengagement in certain areas, tensions remain high, and both sides continue to develop infrastructure and strengthen military capabilities.
 
 
 
• **India's Strategic Response:**
 
 
• India has focused on improving infrastructure in border areas, including roads, tunnels, and airbases to facilitate troop movement and logistics.
 
• The deployment of advanced weaponry and technologies such as drones, fighter jets, and surveillance equipment has enhanced India's preparedness along the LAC.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Galwan Valley Clash:**

 
 
• In June 2020, a violent face-off occurred in the Galwan Valley, resulting in the deaths of **20 Indian soldiers** and an unspecified number of Chinese troops.
 
• This was the first deadly clash between the two nations since **1975**.
 
 
 
• **China's Strategy:**
 
 
• China has been accused of pursuing a policy of "salami slicing" – gradually encroaching on disputed territories to gain strategic advantage.
 
• Its Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and related projects have also raised concerns about its intentions in the region.
 
 
 
• **India's Strategic Partnerships:**
 
 
• To counter China's aggression, India has strengthened ties with nations like the **United States, Japan, and Australia**, forming the **Quad** alliance.
 
• India has also enhanced defense cooperation with Russia and other allies to modernize its armed forces.

questions.question: The governor of a province (bhukti) in the Pala and Pratihara empire was called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uparika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Uparika** was used to designate the **governor of a province (bhukti)** during the **Pala and Pratihara empire**.
 
• In ancient India, provinces or large administrative units were known as **bhuktis**, and the Uparika was responsible for overseeing the administration within these provinces.
 
• The Uparika was generally appointed by the central authority, such as the king or emperor, to ensure proper governance and collection of revenue in the bhukti.
 
• During the reign of the **Pala dynasty**, the administrative structure was highly centralized, and the Uparika played a crucial role in maintaining order and implementing policies at the provincial level.
 
• The **Pratihara empire**, known for its vast territorial expanse, required efficient provincial governance, which was carried out by officials like the Uparika.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Administrative Structure in the Pala and Pratihara Empires:**

 
 
• The Pala empire (8th to 12th century CE) was known for its centralized administrative system, with the king at the apex and officials like **Uparika** managing provinces.
 
• The Pratihara empire (8th to 11th century CE) had a similar structure, with provinces being governed by Uparikas to ensure smooth administration.
 
• Both empires employed a system of revenue collection, and the Uparikas played a key role in ensuring the proper functioning of this system at the provincial level.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Uparika:**
 
 
• Uparika was tasked with maintaining law and order within the province.
 
• He ensured the efficient collection of taxes and revenues from the bhukti and its smaller administrative units, known as **visayas**.
 
• He implemented the policies and orders issued by the central government or the king.
 
• Uparika also oversaw judicial functions and resolved disputes at the provincial level.
 
 
 
• **Other Administrative Titles:**
 
 
• **Rashtrapati:** This term referred to the head of a **Rashtra** (a larger administrative unit), but it was not used for provincial governors in the Pala and Pratihara empires.
 
• **Visayapati:** This title was given to the official in charge of a **visaya** (district or smaller administrative unit).
 
• **Koshtapala:** This term was associated with treasury officials and not the provincial governors.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Pala dynasty ruled over regions of **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha**, while the Pratiharas controlled much of northern India during their reign.
 
• Effective provincial administration was vital for maintaining the vast territories under these empires, and the Uparikas played a significant role in this regard.
 
• These administrative practices set the groundwork for later governance systems in medieval India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bhukti:** Refers to a province or large territorial division within the empire, governed by the Uparika.
 
• **Visayas:** Smaller administrative units within a Bhukti, managed by Visayapatis under the supervision of the Uparika.
 
• **Revenue Collection:** The Uparika ensured the efficient collection of taxes, which were vital for the empire's economy and governance.
 
• **Centralized Administration:** Both the Pala and Pratihara empires relied on centralized governance, with provincial governors ensuring the implementation of policies.
 
• **Judicial Responsibilities:** The Uparika also played a role in resolving disputes and maintaining justice within the province.

questions.question: Which of the following was among the first financial institutions in India to receive an 'in principle' approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to set up a bank in the private sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HDFC Limited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **HDFC Limited** was among the first financial institutions in India to receive the **'in principle' approval** from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to set up a private bank.
 
• It was granted this approval under the **1993 guidelines** issued by the RBI for the establishment of private sector banks.
 
• **HDFC Bank**, a subsidiary of HDFC Limited, was incorporated in **August 1994** and commenced operations as a commercial bank in **January 1995**.
 
• HDFC Bank is known for its **robust digital infrastructure**, providing services like retail banking, wholesale banking, and treasury operations.
 
• Its establishment marked a significant step in the liberalization of India's banking sector, allowing private entities to contribute to financial growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India Guidelines for Private Sector Banks:**

 
 
• In **1993**, the RBI released guidelines allowing private entities to establish banks in India to foster competition and improve efficiency in the banking sector.
 
• These guidelines aimed to increase **financial inclusion** and provide better banking services to the unbanked population.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of HDFC Bank:**
 
 
• HDFC Bank specializes in **retail banking**, offering products such as savings accounts, loans, and credit cards.
 
• It is also known for its advanced **digital banking services**, including mobile banking and net banking platforms.
 
• As of **2023**, HDFC Bank is one of India's largest private banks in terms of market capitalization and customer base.
 
 
 
• **Other Banks Receiving Approval:**
 
 
• **IndusInd Bank Limited:** Established in **1994**, it was also among the first private banks approved under the 1993 guidelines.
 
• **Axis Bank:** Formerly known as UTI Bank, it began operations in **1993**.
 
• **Kotak Mahindra Bank:** Received its banking license in **2003**, becoming India's first non-banking finance company (NBFC) to transform into a bank.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Private Sector Banks:**
 
 
• Private banks have introduced **modern banking practices**, such as ATMs, digital payments, and personalized financial products.
 
• They have significantly contributed to India's economic growth by increasing access to credit and promoting entrepreneurship.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Development of India's Banking Sector:**

 
 
• The introduction of private banks was a part of the **liberalization policies** initiated in the 1990s.
 
• This allowed the banking sector to expand and cater to the growing needs of India's economy.
 
• Private banks have played a pivotal role in **financial innovation** and technology adoption.

questions.question: Women play a significant role in rural livelihoods and household management. What is the minimum percentage of seats reserved for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.33**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Women play a **significant role** in rural livelihoods and household management, contributing substantially to the economic and social fabric of rural areas.
 
• In India, **Article 243D** of the Constitution mandates that at least **one-third (33%) of seats** in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) be reserved for women.
 
• This reservation is aimed at empowering women and increasing their participation in **local governance** and decision-making processes.
 
• The reservation applies to seats at all levels of PRIs, including **Gram Panchayat**, **Block Panchayat**, and **District Panchayat**, ensuring representation across the governance hierarchy.
 
• Several states, such as **Bihar** and **Rajasthan**, have gone beyond the constitutional mandate, reserving **50% of seats** for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs):**

 
 
• PRIs are a system of rural local governance in India, established under the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992**.
 
• They consist of three tiers: **Gram Panchayat** at the village level, **Panchayat Samiti** at the block level, and **Zila Parishad** at the district level.
 
• PRIs aim to decentralize power and bring governance closer to the people, promoting **participatory democracy**.
 
 
 
• **Empowerment of Women:**
 
 
• The reservation of seats for women in PRIs is a crucial step towards achieving **gender equality** in governance.
 
• It helps women gain experience in leadership roles, enhancing their confidence and decision-making abilities.
 
• Studies have shown that women leaders in PRIs often prioritize issues like **education, healthcare, and sanitation**, leading to improved outcomes in these areas.
 
 
 
• **State Initiatives:**
 
 
• States like **Kerala** and **Karnataka** have implemented innovative programs to train women elected representatives in PRIs.
 
• These initiatives aim to enhance the capacity of women leaders, enabling them to effectively perform their duties and address community needs.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:**
 
 
• Despite the reservation, women in PRIs often face challenges such as **patriarchal attitudes**, lack of training, and limited access to resources.
 
• Efforts are needed to address these barriers and ensure that women can fully participate and lead in local governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act:**

 
 
• Introduced in **1992**, this act laid the foundation for the Panchayati Raj system in India.
 
• It added **Part IX** to the Constitution and provided for the establishment of **Gram Sabha** and PRIs.
 
• It also introduced the concept of **reservation** for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women in PRIs.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Women's Reservation:**
 
 
• Women's representation in PRIs plays a critical role in addressing **gender disparities** and ensuring inclusive governance.
 
• It also serves as a platform for women to voice their concerns and contribute to community development.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• India's efforts to ensure women's representation in local governance align with global goals like the **UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly **Goal 5** on achieving gender equality.
 
• Countries like **Rwanda** have also implemented gender quotas in governance, with women holding over **60% of parliamentary seats**.

• **Comparison of Options:**

• **Laws and rituals:** While the Vedas include rituals, they are not codified laws but rather guidelines for spiritual practices.
 
• **Prayers and hymns:** This is the main content of the Vedas, as they consist of hymns dedicated to deities and prayers for prosperity, health, and spiritual growth.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**

• They were transmitted orally for generations before being written down.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of road transport over railways?

options.text: Cheaper and faster than railway transport over long distances

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Door-to-door service**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Road transport** provides **door-to-door service**, which is its primary advantage over railways. This means goods and passengers can be directly picked up from their location and delivered to their destination without the need for intermediate transfers.
 
• Unlike railways that require goods to be transported to and from railway stations, road transport can directly reach areas where railways or other forms of transport may not be accessible.
 
• Road transport is highly **flexible**, as it allows routes and schedules to be altered quickly based on the needs of the user. This is in stark contrast to the fixed routes and schedules of railways.
 
• It is particularly suitable for **short distances** and transporting small quantities of goods. The ability to navigate narrow roads and reach remote locations makes road transport ideal for localized distribution.
 
• Although road transport is not as cost-effective as railways for long distances, it excels in providing **last-mile connectivity**, which railways cannot offer efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Advantages of Road Transport:**

 
 
• **Accessibility:** It can reach remote and rural areas, which are often inaccessible by railways or airways.
 
• **Cost-effectiveness:** For short distances, road transport is usually more economical compared to other modes.
 
• **Flexibility:** Road transport provides flexibility in terms of route, timing, and door-to-door delivery, making it convenient for personalized services.
 
• **Quick and direct:** Unlike railways, road transport does not require loading and unloading at intermediate points, reducing transit time and damage to goods.

• **Loading and unloading:** Goods often need to be transported to and from railway stations, increasing transit time and costs.
 
• **Cost:** Railways are more cost-effective over long distances, but for shorter routes, road transport is more economical and practical.
 
• **Schedule dependency:** Railways operate on fixed schedules, which may not always align with the immediate needs of the users.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Considerations:**
 
 
• Road transport is generally less **environmentally friendly** compared to railways due to higher fuel consumption and emissions.
 
• Electric trains and other eco-friendly rail options are becoming more popular to address environmental concerns.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Road Transport and Railways:**
 
 
• **Road Transport:** Offers flexibility, door-to-door service, and is better for short distances.
 
• **Railways:** More economical and efficient for long distances, especially for bulk goods and passengers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• In India, **road transport handles nearly 65% of freight** and 90% of passenger traffic, demonstrating its importance in the transportation sector.

• One of the core aspects of the movement was the **no-tax campaign**, targeting the oppressive practices of **Indigo planters and zamindars** who exploited peasants.
 
• The Indigo planters were mostly European landlords who forced peasants to grow indigo under exploitative terms, often leading to financial ruin for the farmers.
 
• **Zamindars** were local landlords who collected exorbitant taxes from peasants, often pushing them into extreme poverty.

• **Faraizi Movement:**

 
 
• Founded by **Haji Shariatullah** in Bengal during the early 19th century (around 1819).
 
• The movement derived its name from “Farz,” which means obligatory duties in Islam. It advocated for the observance of Islamic principles and practices.
 
• It addressed both **religious and socio-economic oppression**, focusing on the plight of peasants and their exploitation by landlords and planters.

• The cultivation of indigo was labor-intensive and reduced soil fertility, further worsening the conditions of the farmers.
 
• The exploitation of indigo farmers led to the historic **Indigo Revolt in 1859**, which was one of the first organized peasant movements in India.
 
 
 
• **Zamindari System:**
 
 
• The **Zamindari system** was introduced by the British in Bengal through the **Permanent Settlement Act of 1793**.
 
• Zamindars were given the role of collecting taxes from peasants on behalf of the British government.
 
• Many zamindars exploited peasants by collecting **exorbitant taxes** and seizing their lands in case of non-payment.
 
• The oppressive practices of zamindars were a major cause of rural poverty and led to widespread resentment among farmers.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Faraizi Movement:**
 
 
• It played a crucial role in raising awareness about the rights of peasants and resisting exploitation.
 
• The movement influenced later peasant uprisings such as the **Indigo Revolt** and other agrarian movements in colonial India.
 
• It also contributed to the socio-religious reform efforts among Muslims in Bengal.

• The movement under Haji Shariatullah also contributed to the development of Islamic reform movements in India, emphasizing the importance of socio-economic equality.
 
• The Faraizi Movement was not limited to religious reforms but also addressed the socio-political challenges faced by the Muslim peasantry in Bengal.
 
• Similar peasant movements during colonial times include the **Pagal Panthis** in Bengal and the **Deccan Riots** in Maharashtra.

__
 
• **Werner Heisenberg** is best known for his contribution to the development of **quantum mechanics**, which he published in **1925**.
 
• Heisenberg formulated the **Matrix Mechanics representation** of quantum mechanics, which became one of the foundational frameworks for understanding quantum physics.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for the **Uncertainty Principle**, a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics that describes the limitations of measuring certain pairs of variables simultaneously.
 
• Heisenberg's contributions earned him the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1932** for the creation of quantum mechanics.
 
• Quantum mechanics revolutionized science by providing a deeper understanding of atomic and subatomic particles and their interactions. *Hence, the correct answer is Werner Heisenberg.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Quantum mechanics** is a fundamental branch of physics that deals with the behavior of particles at atomic and subatomic levels.
 
• It describes phenomena that cannot be explained by classical physics, such as the behavior of electrons in an atom or photons of light.
 
• Key principles include the **wave-particle duality**, **superposition**, and **entanglement**.
 
 
 
• **Werner Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle:**
 
 
• The **Uncertainty Principle** states that it is impossible to simultaneously measure both the position and momentum of a particle with perfect accuracy.
 
• This principle highlights the inherent limitations in observing particles at quantum levels.
 
• It has significant implications for fields like quantum computing, cryptography, and particle physics.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributors to Quantum Mechanics:**
 
 
• **Wolfgang Pauli:** Known for the **Pauli Exclusion Principle**, which states that no two fermions can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously.
 
• **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz:** Known for discovering electromagnetic waves but not directly related to the theory of quantum mechanics.
 
• **Ernest Rutherford:** Famous for his gold foil experiment and contributions to nuclear physics, but not associated with the development of quantum mechanics.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Quantum Mechanics:**
 
 
• Quantum mechanics is used in technologies like **semiconductor devices**, **quantum computing**, and **medical imaging** such as MRI.
 
• It also plays a crucial role in understanding chemical bonding, molecular structures, and the behavior of materials.

questions.question: Which one of the following hypotheses/theories explains the formation of the solar system from a rotating cloud of gas and dust?

__
 
• The **Nebular Hypothesis** explains the formation of the solar system from a **rotating cloud of gas and dust**, also known as a nebula.
 
• This hypothesis was first proposed by the German philosopher **Immanuel Kant** in 1755 and later expanded upon by the French mathematician **Pierre-Simon Laplace** in 1796.
 
• According to this theory, the solar system began as a giant rotating cloud of interstellar gas and dust, which began to collapse under its own gravity.
 
• As the cloud contracted, it spun faster, forming a flattened disk with the Sun forming at its center and the planets forming from the remaining matter in the disk.
 
• This hypothesis remains one of the most widely accepted explanations for the formation of the solar system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What is the function of device drivers in an operating system?

• **Device Drivers** act as a crucial software component that facilitates communication between an operating system (OS) and hardware devices like printers, keyboards, or storage drives.
 
• The primary function of device drivers is to translate high-level commands from the OS into low-level hardware-specific instructions that the device can understand and execute.
 
• Drivers work as intermediaries that allow the OS to access and control hardware resources without needing to know the hardware's intricate details.
 
• Examples of device drivers include printer drivers, graphics card drivers, sound card drivers, and network drivers, which ensure proper functioning of their respective devices.
 
• Without device drivers, the operating system would not be able to interact with hardware devices, rendering them non-functional. ***Thus, the correct answer is the second option.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Device Drivers:**

 
 
• **Kernel-mode drivers:** These drivers operate in the kernel space of the operating system and have unrestricted access to hardware resources. Examples include drivers for storage devices and network adapters.
 
• **User-mode drivers:** These run in user space and interact with devices that do not require direct hardware access, such as printers and scanners.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Device Drivers:**
 
 
• They ensure compatibility between the OS and various hardware components, regardless of their manufacturers.
 
• They enable hardware upgrades without necessitating changes in the operating system.
 
• They allow seamless operation of peripherals and improve system performance.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Device Driver Applications:**
 
 
• **Graphics Driver:** Allows the OS to communicate with the GPU for rendering visuals.
 
• **Audio Driver:** Facilitates sound output by managing communication between the sound card and the OS.
 
• **Network Driver:** Enables internet or LAN connectivity by controlling network adapters.
 
 
 
• **Updates and Maintenance:**
 
 
• Regular updates ensure device drivers remain compatible with the latest OS versions and fix bugs or vulnerabilities.
 
• Manufacturers often release driver updates to enhance performance and ensure better hardware utilization.
 
 
 
• **Device Driver Examples:**

• In Linux, device drivers are often integrated into the kernel, such as those for USB devices or network interfaces.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators.

LCM of Fractions

Relationship between LCM and HCF

For any two numbers A and B: LCM × HCF = A × B.

questions.question: The number 648679059 is divisible by which of the following?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To check divisibility by 3, simply calculate the sum of all digits of the given number.

Sum of digits = 6 + 4 + 8 + 6 + 7 + 9 + 0 + 5 + 9 = 54

Since 54 is a multiple of 3 (54 ÷ 3 = 18), the entire number is perfectly divisible by 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 648679059

**Concept Used:**

Check standard divisibility rules for each given option (10, 11, 3, 8) systematically to find the correct match.

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Divisibility by 10:** The last digit must be 0. Here, the last digit is 9, so it is not divisible by 10.

⇒ **Divisibility by 11:** The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

⇒ Sum of digits at odd places = 6 + 8 + 7 + 0 + 9 = 30

⇒ Sum of digits at even places = 4 + 6 + 9 + 5 = 24

⇒ Difference = 30 − 24 = 6. Since 6 is not a multiple of 11, it is not divisible by 11.

⇒ **Divisibility by 8:** The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 8.

⇒ The last three digits form 059, which is not divisible by 8.

⇒ **Divisibility by 3:** The sum of all digits must be divisible by 3.

⇒ Sum = 6 + 4 + 8 + 6 + 7 + 9 + 0 + 5 + 9 = 54

⇒ 54 is completely divisible by 3, confirming the whole number is divisible by 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 4 & 8

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 9

Similar to the rule for 3, a number is completely divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility by 6

A number must be divisible by both 2 (ending in an even digit) and 3 (sum of digits is a multiple of 3) to be perfectly divisible by 6.
</p

questions.question: Find the difference between a single discount of 20% and two successive discounts of 10% and 10% on a gift of ₹600.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between a single discount of 2x% and two successive discounts of x% each is directly given by (x² ÷ 100)%.

Here, the single discount is 20% and the successive discounts are 10% and 10%, so x = 10.

Difference in discount % = (10² ÷ 100)% = 1%.

Difference in value = 1% of ₹600 = ₹6.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Disc = ₹120

 

 Successive: 10% & 10%

 
 Disc = ₹114

 

 Diff = ₹6

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Effective discount for successive x% and y% = [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Case 1: Single discount = 20%

⇒ Case 2: Effective discount for 10% and 10% = 10 + 10 − (10 × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective discount = 20 − 1 = 19%

⇒ Difference in discount percentages = 20% − 19% = 1%

⇒ Difference in discount amount = 1% of ₹600

Successive Discounts

Marked Price & Selling Price

Single vs Successive Disadvantage

For a buyer, a single flat discount is always better than successive discounts adding up to the same total numerical percentage, as successive discounts reduce the base value incrementally.

Simplify fractions and expand the terms directly using mental math.

⇒ 3(2x² − 22x + 14) − 6(x² + 6x − 15)

⇒ 6x² − 66x + 42 − 6x² − 36x + 90

Cancel out the 6x² terms and add the remaining terms:

⇒ −102x + 132

**∴ The correct answer is −102x + 132.**

3((6 ÷ 3)x² − 22x + 14) − 6(x² + 6x − 15)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, simplify the fraction inside the brackets: 6 ÷ 3 = 2

⇒ Substitute this back into the expression:

⇒ 3(2x² − 22x + 14) − 6(x² + 6x − 15)

⇒ Distribute 3 to each term in the first bracket:

⇒ (3 × 2x²) − (3 × 22x) + (3 × 14) = 6x² − 66x + 42

⇒ Distribute −6 to each term in the second bracket:

⇒ (−6 × x²) − (6 × 6x) − (−6 × −15) = −6x² − 36x + 90

⇒ Write the complete expanded expression:

⇒ 6x² − 66x + 42 − 6x² − 36x + 90

⇒ Group the like terms together (x² terms, x terms, and constants):

⇒ (6x² − 6x²) + (−66x − 36x) + (42 + 90)

⇒ 0 − 102x + 132

⇒ −102x + 132

**∴ The correct answer is −102x + 132.**

Always simplify operations inside brackets first. Then proceed with multiplication and division, followed by addition and subtraction.

Distributive Property

When multiplying a number by a bracketed polynomial, multiply the outer number by each individual term inside the bracket: a(b + c) = ab + ac.

Combining Like Terms

In algebra, only terms with the exact same variables and exponents can be added or subtracted together.
